question: How does the Autel EVO Max 4N choose its altitude when it returns home?

intake.decided_by: code (single pass has no intake call)

brief.short_answer: The Autel EVO Max 4N’s manual shows that, on C2 link loss, the drone uses a pre-set Signal Lost action which can be Return to Home, Hover, or Land; however, the manual does not specify how the altitude is chosen during a return-home sequence. It emphasizes reconnection attempts during RTH and that signals lost trigger a configured behavior rather than a fixed altitude rule. There is no explicit altitude-determination rule described in the provided passages. Gaps in altitude behavior remain unresolved by these sources.

sections.label: FAA guidance
sections.abstain_reason: no claims in the single-pass brief

claims.text: On C2 link loss, the drone will execute the preset Signal Lost behavior, which can include Return to Home, Hover, or Land.
claims.quote: The drone will enter a reconnection state when the C2 (Command & Control) link is lost, continuously attempting to re- establish connection with the ground control station... If the link is restored within 10 seconds after disconnection, control will automatically return to the remote controller. If reconnection is not established within 10 seconds, the Autel Enterprise App will display the warning message “Aircraft disconnected,” and the drone will execute the preset Signal Loss Action or Signal Lost behavior accordingly.

claims.text: The Signal Lost behavior options include Return to Home, Hover, and Land.
claims.quote: Signal Lost behavior: Configure how the drone should respond when the C2 link between the drone and the remote controller is lost for more than 10 seconds (e.g., remote controller power-off).

claims.text: There is no explicit description of how altitude is determined during a Return to Home (RTH) sequence in the supplied passages.
claims.quote: During automated flight missions, if the connection between the drone and the remote controller is lost, the drone will continue flying in its current state until the Autel Enterprise App displays the disconnection message. Only then will the drone execute the preset Signal Loss Action.

claims.text: There is an incident report of loss of control after takeoff with no location recovered, implying a failed or unknown altitude outcome.
claims.quote: Shortly after takeoff I completely lost control of the UAS. Platform continued to fly away from me while input into the controls to return. All attempts of Return To Home features failed. UAS Platform has not been located or recovered.

gaps.text: No explicit altitude-selection rule for RTH or Hover during lost-link in the provided manual sections.
No cross-section guidance tying explicit altitude behavior to different Signal Lost actions across sections.
